author: reek
body: A tone says what a widget MEANS and the theme owns which colour that is. The reason this is a render test and not an arithmetic one: a field that nothing reads looks exactly like a working one, so the assertion has to be that the pixels changed, not that the setter stored a number.

author: reek
body: **That is not hypothetical here.** Re-pointed 2026-08-03 from `apps/guios/GopRender.codex`, which was retiring, onto the compositor that ships -- and `GopComposite` was ignoring `wn-tone` entirely. It resolved a style and painted `ws-fg`, so every badge rendered on the real desktop was the same colour whatever it was reporting, which is the entire content of a badge. The field was read by the renderer being deleted and by nothing that shipped. Moving this test is what found it.

author: reek
body: Each arm paints into the same scratch buffer after refilling it with the background, so a count is that arm's ink and not the last one's.
